title: After the uniform CI ruling, nothing runs the suite under bash 3.2 before a tag is pushed
body:
hv's fleet CI ruling, confirmed at Utilz on 2026-09-22 ("Keep things uniform, regardless of public/private repo state"), moves the macOS jobs to release tags and manual runs. Utilz targets bash 3.2 because that is what macOS ships, and the macOS CI legs were the only thing running the suite under it: `/bin/bash bin/utilz test` is bash 3.2 for the dispatcher ALONE, because bats is `#!/usr/bin/env bash` and Homebrew's bash comes first on this machine's PATH (`intent/restart.md`, the traps section, measured 2026-09-14).

So after the ruling the release core's own `test estate` gate, which is every suite and the last gate before a tag, runs bats and every test under bash 5.3.20, and the first 3.2 run of a release happens on the tag's CI, AFTER the core has pushed the tag that the Homebrew formula names. A 3.2 regression would be found by a user's install.

MEASURED HERE 2026-09-22: `bats` is `/opt/homebrew/bin/bats` with an `env bash` shebang, which resolves to 5.3.20; with `/bin` first on PATH the same shebang resolves to 3.2.57, while `git`, `yq` and `gh` still resolve, because Homebrew stays on the path behind `/bin`.

THE FIX IS A WRAPPER, NOT A PREFIX IN THE CONFIG. devbin's gate runner splits a declared `run:` into words and execs it without a shell (`lib/helpers`, `run_words`), so `PATH=... bin/utilz test` in the config would be read as a command named `PATH=...`. Prefixing the whole cut cannot work either: devbin's own floor is bash 5 and it refuses 3.2. So `tools/test-estate` re-execs `bin/utilz test` with `/bin` first on PATH, and `commands.test.options.estate.run` names it. It lives in `tools/` for the same reason `ci-state` does: `bin/` is published, and a release tool there would ship to every install.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLAIM: the gate is still one machine's bash 3.2 on macOS. It does not restore what CI's Linux legs or a second macOS runner prove, and it does not run on a push. It restores the 3.2 run that stood between a green tree and a tag.
